title: Bandits with expert advice: pre-action advice and post-action single-arm feedback.
summary: Each round reveals all experts' distributions over arms before the learner selects an arm and observes only its loss. The target is the best fixed advice expert, whose cumulative benchmark is expected loss under its advice distributions.

description_paragraphs: Each round reveals all experts' distributions over arms before the learner selects an arm and observes only its loss. The target is the best fixed advice expert, whose cumulative benchmark is expected loss under its advice distributions.

model.instance: The environment fixes losses ell_t in [0,1]^K and advice q_{t,i} in the probability simplex for M experts in advance. Each round reveals all current advice before arm selection, then reveals only the chosen arm's loss.

model.parameter_domain_description: $K$: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); $M$: $M\in\mathbb N,\ M\ge K$ (public); $T$: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public).
interaction_timing: Fix q and ℓ in advance.
All $M$ advice vectors for the current round are revealed.
The learner chooses $a_t$ from advice, history, and private randomness.
Incur and observe ℓ_t(a_t), then proceed to the next round.
model.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner’s private seed. This is an oblivious-adversary specification and does not automatically extend to history-dependent adaptive adversaries.
unresolved_applicability: Matching lower bounds for the restricted protocol that selects an expert before seeing advice do not apply to this stronger feedback model. The current gap is retained.
description_paragraphs: Expert i’s current advice distribution $q_{t,i}$ lies in the K-dimensional probability simplex. All M advice distributions are visible before the arm is selected.
The hidden loss vector $\ell_t$ lies in [0,1]^K and is not visible before acting.

The comparator is the best fixed expert in hindsight, $i$, whose cumulative loss is the expected loss of its advice distribution, $\sum_t\langle q_{t,i},\ell_t\rangle$. Experts do not receive separately sampled reward trajectories.
This specification requires $K\ge2$, $M\ge K$, and $T\ge1$, with actions in $[K]$.
Advice is supplied through a dense M-by-K numerical interface; future advice remains hidden.

operations.query_signature: Input: $(q_{t,1},\ldots,q_{t,M})\ \longrightarrow\ a_t\in[K]$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: All current advice is visible before arm selection; the learner need not select an expert before advice is revealed. After acting, only the chosen arm's loss is returned, not the full loss vector or every expert's true loss. Advice and losses are fixed in advance, with no additional observation noise.

operations.coupling: All current advice is visible before arm selection; the learner need not select an expert before advice is revealed. After acting, only the chosen arm's loss is returned, not the full loss vector or every expert's true loss. Advice and losses are fixed in advance, with no additional observation noise.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

public_inputs: All M current advice vectors are revealed before arm selection; future advice is not supplied in advance.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
description_paragraphs: Full advice is revealed first, followed by the selected-arm loss.

$$
(q_{t,1},\ldots,q_{t,M})\ \longrightarrow\ a_t\in[K]\ \longmapsto\ Y_t=\ell_t(a_t)
$$
All current advice is visible before selecting an arm. Selection of an expert before advice is not required.
After acting, only the selected arm's loss is returned, not the full $\ell$_t or the true loss of every expert.
Expert advice and losses are fixed in advance; there is no additional observation noise.
Public inputs are $K,T,M$. All $M$ current recommendation vectors are revealed before arm selection; future recommendations are not supplied.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Both cumulative losses lie in [0,T], so their difference on each execution path lies in [-T,T].

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
Each round reveals M × K advice values and one loss scalar, for T selected-arm feedback observations.
The dense expert-advice interface reveals MK numbers per round and MKT in total. Compressed or structured advice is a different interface.

resource.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
resource.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: Any policy based on the revealed advice is permitted. q-FTRL may maintain expert weights and sample arms from their mixture. Dense advice contains $MK$ numbers per round. Mixing, importance weighting, and solving FTRL subproblems are internal computations, not bandit observations.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
description_paragraphs: Each round reveals M × K advice values and one loss scalar, for T selected-arm feedback observations.
Any policy acting after recommendations are revealed is allowed. q-FTRL may maintain expert weights and sample an arm from their mixture.
Dense advice itself contains MK numbers per round. Mixing, importance weighting, and FTRL subproblems are internal computation and are not hidden inside the bandit sample count.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable computation with exact real arithmetic is permitted; feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. The policy may depend on the revealed advice. q-FTRL may maintain expert weights and sample an arm from their mixture. Dense advice contains $MK$ numbers per round. Mixing, importance weighting, and FTRL subproblems are internal computations and are not absorbed into the bandit sample count.
algorithms.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native objective is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{(q_{t,i}),\ell_{1:T}}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: First take the infimum over complete nonanticipating learning policies using only public inputs.
Then take the supremum over instances fixed before interaction and satisfying the model assumptions.
Expectation includes learner randomness and any sampling or observation noise.
Fixed, per-round, and sample-path comparators are distinguished exactly as in the target expression.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\inf_{\mathcal{A}}\sup_{(q_{t,i}),\ell_{1:T}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}}[R_T]
$$

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

bounds.derivation: Let the first $K$ experts always recommend distinct fixed arms, and let all remaining experts duplicate those recommendations. Revealed advice carries no loss information, and the best-expert comparator becomes the best fixed arm. The finite-armed bandit lower bound therefore applies directly.

evidence.supports: The source supports $\mathcal{R}_T^*\ge0.04\sqrt{KT}$ and the stated reductions, subject to each atomic claim's model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Use only the K-armed bandit branch with source sampling budget $m_{\mathrm{src}}=T$. In context-block reductions each block uses its own length. Bernoulli hard instances and Yao's principle give the randomized-learner lower bound.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\mathcal{R}_T^*\le2\sqrt{eKT\bigl(2+\log(M/K)\bigr)}$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: The source upper bound is $2\sqrt{e(K\wedge M)T(2+\log(M/(K\wedge M)))}$. This setting reveals all expert advice before the action, so it can simulate the feedback required by the proved algorithm.
